The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stated, inter alia, that the original and real owner of the suit land, the SA recorded tenant left this country in 1965 for India leaving this property. The property, thereafter, has been enlisted as vested and non resident property and the same is maintained by the defendant No. 2. Chinta Haran and Provath Chandra were not the citizens of this country and their names were not enlisted in the voter list rather they were the citizens of India. Husband of the plaintiff tried to get lease of the suit property on behalf of his wife admitting that the suit property as vested and non resident property in 1982 by filing application to the then SDO Munshiganj, but the prayer was rejected as the plaintiff was not in possession. Thereafter, the authority has leased out the land in VP Case No. 121 of 1974 and the land is in possession of the lease holders. The suit property is vested and non resident property and is being maintained by the Government; hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. The plaintiff again being dissatisfied with the judgment and decree aforesaid passed by the Appellate Court preferred revisional application and obtained the present Rule as stated above. 

 9. Mr Subrata Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff petitioner, has taken me through the judgments of both the courts and during the argument he has placed the evidence as well as the exhibits and submitted that the deed executed by Provath Chandra Nath in favour of the plaintiff was registered at District Registrar Office Bakharganj on 17-7-1973 under section 30(2) of the Registration Act which was done before the amendment of Registration Act in 1985 legally and validly. The learned Advocate further submitted that the deed executed by Chinta Haran Nath in favour of Sreemoti Indrani Nath, the plaintiff at Sadar Sub-Registrar Office at Dhaka under section 7(2) of the Registration Act and such fact has been specifically endorsed by a 'seal' at the reverse of the deed and such act being done by public authority has evidentiary value and to prove such authority of the Sub-Registrar Sadar, Dhaka needs not to produce any paper as deed itself is containing such 'seal' showing authority and the appellate Court has committed no error of law in coming to the finding "according to section 30(2) of Registration Act any registrar can register any document without regard to the situation in any part of Bangladesh of the property to which the property relates if he is satisfied that there is sufficient cause for doing so." Though the vested and non resident property authority did not challenge the validity of such document either in the written statement or in the evidence but the courts below committed error of law in coming to findings that the plaintiff failed to prove her right and title over the suit land which has not been done according to law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submitted that by an alleged application said to have been made by husband of the plaintiff seeking lease of the suit property, cannot render the title of the vendors invalid as the original owners were not parties to that proceeding and such findings of the courts below are not based on proper appreciation of the law and, as such, coming to the findings that the plaintiff could not prove her right and title over the suit land have committed error of law. The learned Advocate further submitted that the DW 1 categorically stated in his evidence that they could not trace the census list in order to prove the contention to the effect that the property was declared enemy property or vested and non-resident property.

 "11. We now revert back to the consequence of the continuance of Ordinance (1 of 1969). As stated earlier under Laws Continuance Enforcement Order, 1971 all laws in force on March 25, 1971 continued in force in Bangladesh as was consistent with the creation of sovereign Bangladesh and this position in law gets full recognition under President's Order No. 29 of 1972, Bangladesh (Vesting of Property and Assets) Order, 1972, and President's Order No. 48 of 1972 Bangladesh (Adaptation of Existing Bangladesh Laws) Order, 1972. President's Order No. 29 of 1972 vests all properties in the Government of Bangladesh which were vested in or managed by any Board constituted by or under any law or in the former Government of East Pakistan or Pakistan, President's Order No. 48 of 1972 provided for the adaptation of laws which were continued to rend amongst others Central Government or Government of East Pakistan on the Provincial Government or the Government of East Pakistan to refer to the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Then came Ordinance IV of 1974 the Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) (Repeal) Ordinance, 1974 which repealed the Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) Ordinance 1 of 1969 and provided, inter alia, that all enemy property vested in the Custodian of Enemy Property appointed under the provisions of the Defence of Pakistan. Rules continued in force by the said Ordinance shall vest in the Government, meaning Government of Bangladesh. There was another Ordinance No. V of 1974. The Vested and Non Resident Property (Administration) Ordinance 1974, which provided for the management and control of the vested and non-resident properties in the manner set out in the Ordinance. These Ordinances were replaced by Act XLV of 1974, Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provisions) (Repeal) Act, 1974, and Act No. XLVI of 1974 the Vested and Non-Resident Property (Administration) Act, 1974. There had been two subsequent enactments, namely Ordinance XCII of 1976, the Vested and Non-Resident Property (Administration ) Repeal) Ordinance 1976 which repealed the Vested and Non-Resident Property (Administration) Act, 1974 followed by Ordinance XCIII of 1976 the Enemy Property (Continuance of Emergency Provision) (Repeal) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976, which has amended section (3) of Act XLV of 1974 by providing that the properties which had vested in the Government, the right of administration, control, management and disposal of by transfer or otherwise be conferred on the Government or of such officer or authority as the Government may direct. This brings us to the up to date position of the enemy property laws which started with the Promulgation of Emergency and the Defence of Pakistan Ordinance and Rules made thereunder in 1965. We have already indicated that the continuance as a vested enemy property and there is no question of the vesting of the property by provisions other than contained in Rules 181 and 182. The effect of Provisions of Act XLV of 1974 as amended by Ordinance XCII and XCIII of 1976, is that the vesting of the property as enemy property by virtue of Defence of Pakistan Rules in the Custodian or Additional Custodian or the Board continued as vested property in the Government of Bangladesh. The vesting occurred by operation of aforesaid Defence of Pakistan Rules in those authorities and those vested properties as enemy properties as past and closed transaction continued to be so in the Government of Bangladesh and the Government acquired by the aforesaid laws all the right of management, control and disposal of the property by transfer or otherwise. Upon a true construction of the laws aforesaid, we get, that all rights in such property vest in the Government of Bangladesh and the title of the owner of the property remains subject to the overriding power of the Government or, in other words, the title of the owner remains eclipsed or suspended as long as property remains vested in the Government. The consequence is that the Government has all the power of management and disposal of those properties and also the power to release those properties. We, therefore, on facts, find that at first the Appellant firm on 20-9-1965 was declared as enemy property firm under Rule 181, and on 27-10-65 its properties were vested in the Additional Custodian under Rule 182 of the Defence of Pakistan Rules, were made during the currency of Emergency and so we find no error in the decision of the High Court that the firm did come within the definition of 'enemy firm' and so its assets were validity vested in the Additional Custodian as enemy property as vested enemy property, it continued by the successive legislations to remain so first, as enemy property and thereafter as vested property 

 16. On perusal of the judgment of the trial Court, it appears, amongst others, the trial Court held that the suit is not maintainable. The trial Court further held that the registration of the deeds having been registered in different places beyond the jurisdiction of the Sub-Registrar Sirajdikhan, those deeds were not validly done and on the basis of those documents the plaintiff acquired no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The trial Court also held, in deciding issue No.6, that the government may resume the property under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as both plaintiff and the defendant failed to prove the respective contention. The appellate Court, on the other hand, affirmed the judgment of the trial Court and came to the findings: 

 17. On perusal of the judgments of both the courts, it appears that the courts below failed to notice the evidence of DW 1 that the DW 1 could not produce the census list which is the legal foundation for treating the suit property as enemy property or vested and non-resident property. It further appears that the courts below on consideration of the application of the husband of the plaintiff held that the plaintiff's husband as well as the plaintiff admitted the property to be the vested and non resident property but such findings of the Court below are not based on law, inasmuch as by mere admission of a third party as to vested property other than the real owner, such findings have got no basis, inasmuch as the admission of a third party cannot thus disentitle a real owner to claim his title over his own land and such findings do not appeal to any reasons, as such, findings are not based in law. It appears further that the deed by Private that was executed on 17-7-1973 in favour of the plaintiff was registered in Bakerganj, District Registrar Office as contemplated under section 30(2) of the Registration Act before the amendment of Registration Act in 1985 which, in my opinion, had been done legally. The deed executed by Chinta Haran was registered at Sadar Sub-Registrar Office at Dhaka under section 7(2) of the Registration Act and such authority is evident from the reverse of the deed. The registration of the deed made under such authority by a public officer has got evidentiary value. So, the registration of his deed appears to have been done legally. The evidence of DW 1 has clearly indicated that the government failed to prove the legal foundation for enlisting the suit property as enemy property producing the census list and if the foundation goes, in that case, the version of the plaintiff that she purchased the land by 2 registered deeds get support of her interest in the suit property. Over all, on the evaluation of the evidence along with the judgments of both the courts, it has been revealed that the Courts below committed error of law in holding that the plaintiff could not prove her right, title and possession in the suit land which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. It appears further that the plaintiff only sought declaration to the effect that the notice issued by the defendant No.2 dated 11-7-1987 is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff but the courts below, as it appears from the record, made endeavour to settle the title of the plaintiff which apparently was a  approach to the pleadings of the parties. It further reveals that the courts below have made out a third case holding that the Government may resume the land under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as the plaintiff and the defendant failed to prove their respective case but such views cannot be approved rather should be deprecated.
